trust_decision.summary: Decided per repository: a repo configured with signed=true may have its commit or tag content fetched, checked out and consumed only after that exact revision's signature was verified with git verify-commit/verify-tag and matched against the configured allowed_signers.

landing_point.why: The summary says validation is 'late', so an engineer looks first at the ReposCheckSignatures step, which is the only place in the pinned tree that imports signer keys and calls repo.check_signature().

fix_sites.entry_point: kas checkout|build|shell|diff|lock|dump|purge|for-all-repos (SetupReposStep inside the repo_setup_loop, which checks out repos needed for includes)
RepoImpl.checkout (kas/repos.py:492-558) reached from both commands above; also legacy refspec and patch-prep refs
new SignatureValidator helper in kas/repos.py, called from both command classes above
fix_sites.module_kind: helper class added to the VCS module (not the command module)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The git command builder in kas/repos.py is not where signature verification lives; the fix message is about validation ordering, so the extra ref-resolution guard can be argued to be unrelated hardening that the report never asked for.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Ref-name precedence must stay untouched for ordinary names: a tag and a branch may legitimately share a name and kas must still check out the tag, and a repo that is not yet cloned must be fetched before git verify-commit can run. Appending '^{commit}' to every intended ref, or a loose regex (the published regex is mis-grouped: '^[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64}$' also matches anything ending in 64 hex chars), redirects or breaks these legitimate checkouts.

O6_input_shapes: signed repo reached through an include-expanded config (SetupReposStep loop) versus through the top-level config (ReposCheckout)
pinned by commit (git verify-commit) versus by tag (git verify-tag)
pinned by branch, or by deprecated refspec, where the verified target is a resolved revision and not the config value
ref operand that is a full 40/64-hex string and can also name a branch, versus an ordinary ref name
unsigned repos and local url-less repos, which must be skipped without requiring signer keys

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second git checkout invocation (prepare_patches_cmd) that builds its ref from commit/tag/branch/refspec
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer hardening 'git checkout' operands would plausibly add the same ref/identity guard to the patch-preparation checkout.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: MercurialRepo as a second VCS implementation with its own checkout_cmd and an is_signed_cmd that raises NotImplementedError
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Signature support is documented as 'Git only' in the schema, so a maintainer could later implement hg verification in the mirrored class and forget the ordering/identity rules.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: signer key material read from another repo's working tree before that repo has been verified
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Keys must be imported before any repo can be verified, so a 'verify the repo that provides the key first' guard is a natural but tricky sibling a maintainer could add here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an alternate consumer that runs arbitrary commands inside every repo working tree
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It consumes repo content after setup, so a maintainer could plausibly add a 'refuse to operate in an unverified signed repo' check in this plugin.

O9_family: improper verification of cryptographic signature before the signed artefact is used (CWE-347), with a time-of-check/time-of-use ordering cause and a ref-identity ambiguity

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools (setup.py), pip, pytest; external binaries git (required), hg (optional), gpg and openssh/ssh-keygen for signature tests; python-gnupg optional
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_signature_verify.py (kas checkout against signed gpg/ssh repos, invalid key and key-retention cases; some cases are marked online for keyserver access), tests/test_refspec.py (ref/tag/branch resolution, test_tag_branch_same_name), tests/test_includehandler.py:158-215 (signers schema constraints), tests/test_commands.py and tests/test_build.py exercise the command pipeline

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move ReposCheckSignatures before ReposCheckout in the Macro setup list (kas/libcmds.py:85-86), which fixes the top-level config path only and leaves the include-driven checkout in SetupReposStep and the ambiguous git checkout <sha-like ref> in checkout_cmd open.
